blocks.content: The Governing Council serves as the premier body tasked with evolving a shared vision of national development priorities, sectors and strategies with the active involvement of States.

rows: No power to allocate central funds to states
Had powers to allocate funds to ministries and state plans
Direct participation in policy formulation from stage one
States interacted mostly through NDC after draft plans were made

items: Chief Ministers of Union Territories with legislative assemblies (Delhi, Puducherry, J&K) are ex-officio members of the Governing Council alongside State CMs.
NITI Aayog and its Governing Council operate on a 'Bottom-Up' approach, unlike the 'Top-Down' approach of the erstwhile Planning Commission.
The Governing Council does not possess financial powers to allocate funds to states; power resides with the Ministry of Finance.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Governing Council of NITI Aayog is the premier body tasked with evolving a shared vision of national development priorities, sectors, and strategies.

It comprises the Prime Minister as Chairperson, Chief Ministers of all States, Chief Ministers of Union Territories with Assemblies (Delhi, Puducherry, J&K), and Lt. Governors of other Union Territories.
It promotes Cooperative Federalism by enabling active and continuous participation of states in the formulation of national development policies.
Reconstructed to replace the role previously held by the National Development Council (NDC) in national strategy formulation.
